practice_description.medium: Performance, software, installation, surveillance systems, social interfaces, web-based work
practice_description.practice_summary: Artist and creator of p5.js who makes performances and installations exploring social relationships mediated by technology. She builds functioning social systems and interfaces as artworks -- becoming a human Amazon Alexa, offering herself as a social media follower, and creating surrogate relationships -- turning protocols of care, surveillance, and connection into artistic material.
practice_description.methodology: McCarthy builds custom software platforms and then performs within them, collapsing the distinction between artist, system, and user. She codes functional surveillance and smart-home systems, then inhabits them as a human operator -- performing the role of AI to expose what automation obscures about care, labor, and intimacy. Her background is in computer science (MIT Media Lab MFA, UCLA professor), and she brings engineering rigor to conceptual art practice. She collaborates with participants who consent to being observed, followed, or cared for by her systems.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: McCarthy's practice models how social protocols and interfaces function as artistic medium. Her work demonstrates that the system design itself -- the rules of engagement between people mediated by technology -- is the artwork, directly relevant to how a graph-curated exhibition might structure relationships between artworks and audiences.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes -- p5.js is literally substrate that thousands of other artists build upon. Her performance systems (LAUREN, Follower) create frameworks that structure social interaction, functioning as ground layers for emergent human behavior.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes -- her work is fundamentally relational. LAUREN creates a surveillance/care relationship between McCarthy and household inhabitants. Follower creates an asymmetric social relationship. Surrogate creates an intimate proxy relationship. The social protocol between participants IS the composition.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Yes -- all her performance works evolve in real time based on participant behavior and social dynamics. The systems respond to and are shaped by the people within them. Each performance instance is unique because human participants bring unpredictable input.

works.title: LAUREN
works.description: McCarthy installed custom smart-home devices in participants' homes, then remotely watched and controlled their environment (lights, appliances, music) as a human Amazon Alexa. Participants consented to 24/7 observation. McCarthy performed care, surveillance, and domestic labor through the interface.
works.relevance: Paradigmatic protocol art: the smart-home system is the artwork, and the social relationship it creates between watcher and watched is the medium. Demonstrates how infrastructure design shapes intimacy and power -- directly relevant to how exhibition systems structure audience relationships.

works.title: p5.js
works.description: Open-source JavaScript library for creative coding, making Processing accessible on the web. Created and led by McCarthy with a community-driven development model emphasizing accessibility and inclusion. Used by millions of artists, designers, and students worldwide.
works.relevance: The most successful example of art infrastructure as commons: a creative tool built as open-source public good that enables an entire ecosystem. Demonstrates how protocol/infrastructure design IS a creative act with massive downstream generative effects.

works.title: Follower
works.description: Web application where users could sign up to be followed by a stranger (McCarthy or a performer) for a day. The follower tracked the participant through public space, documenting the experience. Explored surveillance, social media 'following,' and the desire to be seen.
works.relevance: Turns a social media protocol ('following') into physical performance, revealing the embodied implications of digital social structures. Models how abstract graph relationships (follower/followed) have real spatial and emotional consequences.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: McCarthy is one of the most direct practitioners of protocol art in the social register. She builds functioning technological systems -- smart homes, following apps, surrogate platforms -- and then performs within them, treating the interface design and social protocol as the primary artistic medium. The rules of engagement between people, mediated by her custom software, are the artwork.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: p5.js (open-source creative coding library used by millions); LAUREN smart-home surveillance/care system; Follower social tracking platform; Surrogate intimacy mediation platform; Vibe Check (AI-mediated social interaction system); various custom web applications and IoT systems.

commons_orientation.licence_model: Open source (p5.js is LGPL); artworks vary
commons_orientation.commons_summary: McCarthy has built one of the most important commons resources in creative technology: p5.js is fully open-source, community-governed, and explicitly designed for accessibility and inclusion. She led a community-driven contributor model that prioritized diversity. Her art practice, while not always open-source, operates in the spirit of shared infrastructure -- creating systems that others can participate in and that expose the social contracts underlying technology.

governance_model.governance_detail: p5.js is community-governed with a contributor model, steering committee, and emphasis on inclusive participation -- McCarthy stepped back from lead role to enable community ownership. Her art performances involve negotiated consent with participants but are ultimately directed by McCarthy. She operates between solo artistic vision and community stewardship depending on the project.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Consent is a central theme and material in her work. LAUREN participants explicitly consented to 24/7 surveillance. Follower participants signed up voluntarily. The tension between consent and vulnerability is often the subject of the work -- what does it mean to consent to being watched, followed, or cared for by a stranger? Consent protocols are designed into each piece.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Hybrid -- McCarthy is sole author of the system designs and performances, but participants are essential co-creators whose behavior shapes each work. p5.js has distributed authorship across a global community of contributors. Machine co-authorship appears in later works incorporating AI.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Performance works like LAUREN and Follower have defined durations (days to weeks of active surveillance/following). Each performance is a finite durational event shaped by real-time participant behavior. p5.js is continuously evolving as ongoing infrastructure. Web-based works persist as accessible platforms.

data_materiality.data_sources: Live surveillance feeds (audio, video, environmental sensors) from participants' homes; GPS tracking data; social media behavior; participant communications; web interaction data; sensor data from custom IoT devices.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Consented -- participants voluntarily opt into observation and tracking. The ethical complexity of this consent (can you truly consent to 24/7 surveillance?) is itself artistic material. Data is self-generated through the performance system rather than scraped.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: McCarthy's work does not directly engage with embedding or latent spaces in the technical ML sense. However, her practice navigates social 'latent spaces' -- the hidden structures of care, surveillance, and intimacy that underlie technological interfaces. Later works like Vibe Check incorporate AI/ML components.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes -- works span video surveillance, audio monitoring, physical space, web interfaces, IoT sensor data, and embodied performance. Not unified in a single embedding space but multimodal in practice.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: LAUREN transforms private domestic space into surveilled performance venue. Follower activates public urban space. Gallery installations often include live feeds, screens showing surveillance footage, and interactive web interfaces. Works exist simultaneously in physical space, digital platforms, and the social/relational space between participants.

interoperability.composability: High for p5.js -- it is a library explicitly designed for composability, extensibility, and integration with other web technologies. Art performances are self-contained systems but produce documentation (video, data) that could serve as input elsewhere.
interoperability.technical_openness: p5.js is fully open-source and documented. Performance systems use custom code that is not typically released publicly, though methodology is well-documented through talks and writing.

technical_approach.stack: JavaScript (p5.js, Node.js), web technologies (WebRTC, WebSocket), custom IoT/smart home hardware, surveillance cameras, environmental sensors, GPS tracking, cloud infrastructure, Python, machine learning frameworks for later AI-incorporating works.

network_position.scene_affiliation: Creative coding community (central figure via p5.js); UCLA Design Media Arts (professor); MIT Media Lab alumni; Processing Foundation; new media art / performance art intersection; surveillance art; Ars Electronica; LACMA; Whitney Museum; MoMA; international new media festivals.
network_position.connections: Casey Reas and Ben Fry (Processing, which p5.js extends); Zach Lieberman (creative coding); Kyle McDonald (ML art); Hito Steyerl (surveillance art discourse); connected to broader creative coding ecosystem including Daniel Shiffman (Coding Train), Allison Parrish, and the Processing Foundation community.

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: McCarthy's dual practice -- building commons infrastructure (p5.js) and creating protocol art (LAUREN, Follower) -- directly models what A(DAI) aspires to. She understands how system design shapes creative possibility, how open-source communities are governed, and how social protocols function as artistic medium. Could advise on how A(DAI)'s graph infrastructure might structure social/creative relationships, and her experience leading p5.js governance is directly relevant to commons stewardship.
